source_notes: The inspected version is arXiv:2107.01305v2. Its source identity is pinned; this record does not assert that its numbering is identical to the publisher version.
The previous acquisition checkpoint stopped at page 20. Direct inspection found the Conclusion on page 21 above Appendix A; the inventory boundary was corrected before finalization.

Theorem 2.2 has five numbered equations, (2.7)-(2.11), and all remainder and derivative bounds are retained. Its leading-term definitions are linked to the same theorem because it both defines and uses them; other auxiliary remainders and coefficients remain locally bound.
Theorem 2.7 has three nested subparts under (a), followed by a projected replacement clause. V_k and W_k are bound inside the theorem rather than confused with the calligraphic moment varieties.
Theorem 2.11(b) restricts the landscape to the stated open ball for every fixed B>0; Theorem 2.13(b) restricts only its converse in the stated way. These quantifiers and distinctions are preserved.

Remark 2.9 supplies a specific generic-gradient-span condition for Theorems 2.7, 2.11 and 2.13. Its printed full projected-algebra notation is retained despite the main text explicitly defining only the degree-indexed projected subalgebras.
Theorem 3.3 retains both expressions for s3, all summation constraints and all coefficients, including 1/48 in the first expression and 1/12 in the second.

The spherical and cryo-EM coefficient vectors remain distinct. Their shared Clebsch-Gordan convention is linked separately; the cryo-EM contraction does not acquire a dependency on the spherical-registration model.
Theorem 4.6 and Theorem 4.10 locally bind the piecewise function d(S_l); it is not treated as a separate reusable definition. Their different radial lower bounds are preserved.
The projected model has an additional radial choice ensuring projected-basis orthonormality; arbitrary unprojected orthonormal radial systems are not asserted to suffice.
The introduction, corollaries and proof discussions do not create additional inventory entries or theorem-statement dependencies.
